findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows 5 transformer pads without dimension callouts or clearance annotations. Visual analysis of the 1" = 20' scale drawing estimates distances: Pad 1 approximately 30-40 feet from Bldg 1; Pad 2 approximately 15-20 feet from Bldg 2; Pad 3 approximately 10-15 feet from Bldg 8; Pad 4 approximately 5-10 feet from both Bldg 4 and Bldg 5; Pad 5 approximately 10-15 feet from Bldg 7. No explicit dimension lines, measurement annotations, or written clearance specifications are shown on the plans. No reference to AE Design-approved pad detail sheets that would specify minimum clearance compliance.
findings.reasoning: While visual estimates suggest some pads may comply with the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement (Pads 1, 2, 3), the plans do NOT include actual dimension lines or clearance annotations to definitively confirm the requirement is met. The conservative pass/fail logic requires affirmative evidence (dimension callouts or clearance markings) that the requirement is met, not visual estimation. Pad 4, at approximately 5-10 feet from two buildings, is particularly ambiguous without precise dimensions. The applicant must demonstrate compliance through documented dimensions, not visual approximation.
findings.comment: Transformer pad clearances from buildings are not dimensionally documented on the plans. No dimension lines or clearance callouts are shown to verify the 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from buildings and building foundations. Provide dimension annotations on the electrical plan clearly showing the minimum 5-foot clearance from each building, or reference AE Design-approved pad detail sheets demonstrating compliance.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows Pads 1, 2, and 3 each positioned immediately adjacent to pedestrian sidewalks running around the building perimeter. Visual analysis at 1" = 20' scale estimates these pads are approximately 2-5 feet from the back of the sidewalk. No dimension callouts are provided to document the exact clearance from the back of the sidewalk to the pad edge. The code requires 'minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks,' but the plans do not explicitly annotate this clearance.
findings.reasoning: While the visual estimate suggests the pads may be at or near 2 feet from the sidewalk (meeting the minimum), the plans provide no dimensional annotation to confirm this. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 2-foot minimum is met, not visual estimation. The pads appear to be within or very close to the sidewalk setback zone, creating ambiguity about whether they meet the 2-foot requirement.
findings.comment: Transformer pads positioned adjacent to pedestrian sidewalks (Pads 1, 2, 3) lack documented clearance dimensions from the back of the sidewalks. Provide dimension lines and callouts on the electrical plan showing the minimum 2-foot clearance from the back of sidewalks to each transformer pad, or demonstrate through AE Design approval that the configuration meets code.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 does not document the direction of transformer access doors for any of the five pads, nor does it show the required 10-foot hot-stick use area clearance. Visual analysis shows: Pad 1 is approximately 2-5 feet from a sidewalk curb edge and approximately 5-10 feet from the main entry drive; Pad 4 is approximately 5-10 feet from Buildings 4 and 5 on both sides; Pad 5 is approximately 2-5 feet from a parking drive lane. The regulations require a 10-foot clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent building/structure. Without documented access door orientation and clearance dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: The code specifies that the hot-stick use area (access door side) must have minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. The plans do not identify which side of each pad is the access door side, nor do they document the clearance distance. Pads positioned 5-10 feet from buildings or 2-5 feet from sidewalks/parking areas may violate this requirement if the access door faces the nearby structure. The burden is on the applicant to document both access door location and clearance verification.
findings.comment: Hot-stick use area clearances (minimum 10 feet from access door side) are not documented on the electrical plan. For each transformer pad, clearly indicate which side the access door is located on and provide dimension callouts showing the minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure. Verify compliance with AE Design specifications.

applicableAreas: Areas within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment or 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution
findings.observation: Sheet 32 (Tree List) provides tree inventory with functional categories (M=Mitigation, PL=Parking Lot, SY=Street Yard) but does NOT list specific tree species names. Without species identification, utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) column cannot be verified. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows tree symbols distributed across the site but does not cross-reference species against ECM Appendix F. Trees are present in the vicinity of transformer pads and electrical easements, but species-specific verification of utility compatibility is not documented on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 and ECM Appendix F require verification that trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment are utility-compatible species. The plans identify trees only by functional category (M, PL, SY), not by species name. The requirement cannot be verified without species identification. This is particularly important because the plans do not document whether trees identified as 'M' (mitigation trees) planted specifically for the development are utility-compatible, or whether existing trees within 10 feet of pads meet the requirement.
findings.comment: Tree species planted or retained within 10 lateral feet of transformer pads are not identified by scientific/common name on the landscape or tree list sheets. Provide a cross-referenced list showing each tree's species and confirmation of utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designation for all trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment.

applicableAreas: Trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment
findings.observation: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show any root barrier details or specifications. Tree list (Sheet 32) identifies mitigation trees ('M' designation) distributed throughout the site, including near electrical easements and transformer locations. At 1" = 20' scale, trees shown in vicinity of transformer pad areas (within estimated 20-foot radius) include marked 'M' trees. However, no root barrier dimensions (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment) are documented on the landscape details or specifications.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, 5 feet from equipment) for trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. The landscape plan does not show root barriers anywhere. The absence of any root barrier callouts or detail references on sheets showing landscape elements near transformers and electrical easements suggests this requirement is not being addressed.
findings.comment: Root barriers for trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pads are not documented on the landscape plan. The landscape plan and details must include dimensions and specifications for root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from pad-mounted equipment) for all trees within 20 lateral feet of transformers. Provide detail references and installation specifications on the landscape plan.

applicableAreas: Transformer pads adjacent to designated fire lanes
findings.observation: Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) identifies fire lanes as a continuous loop driveway marked with red curbing and white 'FIRE ZONE' stenciling throughout the property. Sheet 21 shows transformer pads positioned immediately adjacent to this main circulation loop: Pad 1 is at the primary entrance curve of the fire lane; Pads 2 and 3 are along the western edge adjacent to sidewalks that parallel the fire lane; Pad 5 is positioned north of the southern portion of the fire lane loop. The code requires minimum 15-foot clearance from fire lanes. Dimensional annotations are not provided to document compliance with this clearance requirement.
findings.reasoning: The fire lane is the primary circulation drive on the site, and visual analysis shows transformer pads are positioned immediately adjacent to (within 5-10 feet of) this marked fire lane at multiple locations. The code specifies a minimum 15-foot clearance from designated fire lanes. Without dimensional annotations verifying that each pad maintains 15-foot separation from the fire lane loop, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: Transformer pads positioned adjacent to designated fire lanes lack documented 15-foot clearance dimensions. Provide dimension callouts on the electrical plan and fire protection plan showing the minimum 15-foot clearance from each transformer pad to the designated fire lane loop, or verify through AE Design approval that the configuration meets code requirements.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to water service lines
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows water line routing (-W- designated lines) and Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electric lines. Both sheets depict utilities and pads in close proximity throughout the site, but no specific dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between the water lines and transformer pads at any location. The plans do not document horizontal clearance distances required to verify the minimum 5-foot separation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to water lines. The utility and electrical plans show both utilities on the same sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met, not general visual indication of separation.
findings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to water service lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the utility and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all water service lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to wastewater lines
findings.observation: Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) shows wastewater line routing (-WW- designated lines) and Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electric lines. Both sheets depict utilities and pads, but no specific dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between wastewater lines and transformer pads. The plans do not document horizontal clearance distances required to verify the minimum 5-foot separation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to wastewater lines. The utility and electrical plans show both utilities on the same sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met.
findings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to wastewater service lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the utility and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all wastewater service lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to storm drain lines
findings.observation: Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) show storm drain infrastructure (-SD- designated lines) and transformer pads on the site. Both drawings depict utilities and pads in close proximity, particularly near the northeastern portion where the biofiltration/detention pond and storm infrastructure are concentrated. No dimension callouts or clearance measurements are provided between storm drain lines and transformer pads to document compliance with the minimum 5-foot separation requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.B.2 requires minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines. The storm and electrical plans show both utilities on coordinated sheets but provide no dimensional annotation to verify clearance compliance. Conservative pass/fail logic requires documented evidence (dimension lines/callouts) that the 5-foot minimum is met.
findings.comment: Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearances from transformer pads to storm drain lines are not dimensionally documented. Provide dimension callouts on the storm sewer and electrical plans showing the minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to all storm drain lines, measured from pad edge to pipe centerline or outer diameter.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to other underground utilities
findings.observation: Multiple utility sheets show water, wastewater, storm drain, and electric utility routing. However, no cross-utility dimension callouts are provided showing the minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance between transformer pads and other underground utilities (conduits, telephone, cable, reclaimed water, etc.). The utility tap plan and electrical plan show general routing but lack specific clearance documentation between different utility types adjacent to transformer pad locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities (except gas, fuel, steam - which have different clearance requirements). Without dimensional annotation on the plans documenting these clearances at specific locations where utilities cross or run parallel to transformer pads, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearances from transformer pads to other underground utilities are not documented. Provide detail cross-sections and dimension callouts showing the minimum 12-inch clearance from each transformer pad to all other underground utilities (conduits, telephone, cable, etc.), including both horizontal and vertical separations measured from pad edge to utility centerline or outer diameter.

applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to overhead distribution lines
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows an overhead electric line (-OHE-) designated on the southern property boundary. The general notes (Sheet 3) reference electric transmission clearance requirements, specifying '25 feet of transmission structures; 20-foot clearance for aerial equipment/staging.' However, no dimension callouts or cross-section drawings are provided on Sheet 21 to document the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from transformer pad locations to the overhead conductors. The plans do not indicate whether transformer pads are located within the clearance zone of the overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead distribution primary, neutral, and secondary conductors extending from ground to sky. Without dimensional annotation or cross-section drawings showing that transformer pads are positioned beyond this clearance envelope, compliance cannot be verified. The presence of overhead lines on the property adjacent to transformer locations requires explicit clearance documentation.
findings.comment: Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from transformer pads to overhead distribution conductors is not documented. Provide dimension callouts and/or cross-section drawings on the electrical plan showing the clearance from each transformer pad to the nearest overhead distribution line conductor, verifying the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance.

applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows an overhead electric line (-OHE-) on the southern property boundary. The code requires minimum 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors, measured from the conductor centerline (not pole centerline). No dimension callouts are provided on the electrical plan to document the 15-foot radius clearance from transformers to the primary/neutral conductors. The distance from transformer pads to the overhead line location is not dimensionally verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes a 15-foot radius clearance requirement from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. This is a radial clearance measured from the conductor itself, not from the pole. Without specific dimension callouts showing that transformer pads are positioned beyond this 15-foot radius from the conductor location, compliance cannot be confirmed. The overhead line is present on the property adjacent to transformer locations, requiring explicit clearance documentation.
findings.comment: Minimum 15-foot radius clearance from transformer pads to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors is not documented. Provide dimension callouts on the electrical plan showing the radial distance (measured from conductor centerline, not pole) from each transformer pad to the nearest primary and neutral conductor, verifying the minimum 15-foot radius clearance.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with potential overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas
findings.observation: Review of all 39 sheets in the primary site plan revealed no cross-section drawings specifically showing vertical clearances at transformer pad locations. The site plan shows buildings with various heights (33'-5" to 36'-1"), parking levels, and enclosed structures, but no cross-sections are provided to demonstrate vertical clearance compliance at transformer locations. The general notes reference cross-section requirements for other utilities (e.g., drainage, conveyance), but no cross-sections are provided specifically showing vertical clearances from transformer pads to overhead structures, parking garage levels, or enclosed areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes survey and design requirements for clearances from AE facilities to structures. Transformer pads located between buildings or adjacent to parking areas (particularly Pad 4 between Bldgs 4-5, and Pad 5 near parking) warrant vertical clearance verification through cross-section drawings. The absence of any cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at these locations is a clear failure to document compliance with this requirement. The code requires demonstrating that overhead structures, building eaves, or parking structures do not create vertical clearance violations.
findings.comment: Cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at transformer pad locations are not provided on the site plan. For each transformer pad location where overhead structures, building elements, or parking structures are present above or adjacent to the pad, provide cross-section drawings (drawn at adequate scale and clearly labeled) demonstrating the required vertical clearances from the pad to any overhead features.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 (southwest location) relative to vault easement
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 identified a 'Vault Easement' callout immediately adjacent to Transformer Pad 3 in the southwest section of the site. The electrical plan does not document whether the transformer pad is located within the vault easement, adjacent to it, or what clearance is maintained. No notation indicates whether this pad has been approved by Austin Energy Design for placement in relation to the vault easement. The plans do not show the precise boundaries of the vault easement relative to the pad location.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 prohibits transformer pads from being placed in drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, or electrical easements under overhead lines without AE Design written approval. While the plan shows a 'Vault Easement' near Pad 3, it is unclear whether the pad is within the easement boundary or what approvals have been obtained. If the pad is in a prohibited easement without documented approval, this is a deficiency.
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 3 is located adjacent to a Vault Easement callout, but the exact spatial relationship is not documented. Clarify whether the transformer pad is within, adjacent to, or separate from the Vault Easement. If the pad is located within any easement (drainage, water, sewer, or electrical), provide documentation of Austin Energy Design written approval for placement in that easement.

findings.observation: Review of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) and the full site plan set reveals no explicit transformer easement boundaries, widths, or callouts shown around any of the five transformer pads. The plans do not identify specific easement areas reserved for Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance around the pads. While electrical easements are shown at certain property locations (e.g., 5' Electric Easement near Pads), no dedicated transformer pad easements with specified widths are documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 indicates that 'additional clearance and access easements may be required' for AE facilities. This grouping's Regulatory Overview states 'Transformer easements required around pads (width determined by AE Design for accessibility).' The absence of any easement boundaries, dimensions, or callouts specifically designating transformer pad easements on the plans indicates that this requirement has not been addressed. The applicant must demonstrate that the necessary easements have been reserved.
findings.comment: Transformer pad easements are not shown or documented on the electrical plan. Establish and document transformer pad easements around all five pads with dimensions and widths specified by Austin Energy Design to provide the required access for equipment maintenance and accessibility. Show these easements clearly on the electrical plan with dimensions and callouts.

applicableAreas: Electrical service routing from transformers to meters
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads and electrical routing with meter locations labeled on building walls, but no notation documents whether 100% of the electrical service routing from transformers to meters is on private property. The plans show building locations and some meter positions but do not explicitly annotate or verify that underground electric lines routing from each transformer pad to corresponding meters do not cross into public right-of-way or property lines. The routing paths are not dimensionally verified as being fully on private property.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 requires that 'Electrical routing from transformer to meter must be 100% on private property.' The electrical plan shows general routing of underground electric lines but provides no annotation confirming that each service line from transformer to meter remains entirely on private property. Without explicit notation or dimension documentation showing that all routing is beyond property lines and not crossing into right-of-way or adjacent properties, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Electrical service routing from transformer pads to meter locations is not documented as being 100% on private property. Provide annotations on the electrical plan confirming that all underground electric lines from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter remain entirely on private property and do not cross property lines or public right-of-way. Dimension the service routing paths to verify private property placement.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 depicts the five transformer pads as simple rectangular boxes without any dimension annotations (length × width), no pad specification callouts (e.g., '10'×10''), and no reference to AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan provides no electrical specifications document, transformer schedule, or AE Design approval letters. The plan notes reference Austin Energy Design reviews (per Electric Review section), but no ESPA documents, transformer pad detail sheets, or AE Design-approved specifications are included in the accessible documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 and the grouping description require that transformer pad dimensions match Austin Energy Design-approved specifications for the specified service type. The plans provide no dimensions whatsoever and no reference to AE Design detail sheets. The applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with this requirement without showing that the pad dimensions match AE Design specifications. The absence of any dimension callouts or reference to AE Design details constitutes a clear deficiency.
findings.comment: Transformer pad dimensions are not specified on the electrical plan. Provide the pad dimensions (length × width) for each transformer and reference the corresponding AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheet for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase), demonstrating that the pad configuration matches AE Design specifications.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 and visual analysis show Pad 5 located in the southeast section of the site, positioned approximately 2-5 feet north of the southern driveway/parking lane. The Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) shows this area is part of the main circulation and parking zone. The code requires bollards (4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts) when transformer pads are installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle routes. Pad 5's estimated 2-5 foot distance from the parking drive lane indicates it falls within the 4-foot bollard requirement threshold. However, no bollard specifications, locations, or detail references are shown on the site plan.
findings.reasoning: Based on visual analysis, Pad 5 is estimated to be 2-5 feet from a parking drive lane, placing it within the 4-foot triggering distance for bollard installation. The absence of any bollard callouts, specifications, or detail references on the electrical plan or construction details sheets suggests the requirement is not being addressed. Without explicit bollard documentation showing their location, spacing, and specifications per AE Design equipment pad details, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 5, located within 4 feet of a parking/circulation drive lane, requires bollard protection. No bollard specifications, locations, or details are shown on the electrical plan or construction details. Provide dimension callouts and detail references (per AE Design equipment pad details) showing 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards installed to protect the transformer pad, with spacing that allows equipment door opening.
